pre.text: ✅ Directions : You will be listening to ATC instructions and making calls of your own. Most questions ask you to do **more than read back.** Some questions continue from the question before, so keep your notes. Your callsign is HL123. "Say again (=Repeat)" available once only. * Response time for each question : 20 or 30 seconds, as shown

body.text: LIDRO

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, cleared direct LIDRO, descend to 9,000 feet, expect one five minutes of delay.
You are now on the way to LIDRO. You want to know how much delay to expect now.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 7,000 feet. The aircraft ahead has just gone around, so your delay will be longer.
Give a full readback, tell him what you were told earlier, and inquire how long the delay will be now.
Your cabin crew are still securing the cabin. For the next three minutes the highest rate of descent you can accept is 1,500 feet per minute.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, descend to flight level two four zero, two five hundred feet per minute or greater.
Give a full readback, and tell him what you can do instead.
Your performance figures today are for the full length of runway zero nine, so you cannot depart from Mike three. You want to go to holding point Mike one.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi to holding point Mike three via Tango, hold short of runway zero nine.
Give a full readback, and make a request with a reason.
During your landing roll you saw a large dog on the grass beside taxiway Delta. You were busy and you have not reported it. You want the controller to know.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi to stand two two via Kilo, give way to the Airbus A380 on your left.
Give a full readback, and report what you saw.

You are level at flight level one six zero, 40 miles from Wexcombe. A cabin crew member has a serious burn on one hand from the galley oven. You want the controller to know about it. Contact Wexcombe Approach.
Report your status.
You want to land at Wexcombe on the next available runway, with a medical team at the stand.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, turn left heading one three zero, descend to 6,000 feet, vectors for Wexcombe. Say your intentions.
Give a full readback, and say your intentions.
You are at stand one eight at Alderton, ready to push back. You want pushback and start-up. Contact Alderton Ground.
Make a request.
Just after your call, dispatch tells you that a passenger has not boarded and that their bags must be offloaded. It will take one two minutes.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, hold position. Report when you are ready. I have an inbound for your stand in about one zero minutes.
Give a full readback, acknowledge his situation, and tell him how long you need with a reason.
You were on the ILS runway one eight at Pembury. At 800 feet you lost one five knots in windshear and you went around. You are now passing 2,000 feet. Contact Pembury Approach.
Report your status.
You want to hold for two zero minutes until the weather has passed.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, climb to 4,000 feet, turn right heading three six zero. Two things — how much airspeed did you lose, and do you want another approach, or do you want to hold?
Give a full readback, and answer both of his questions.

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In each question you are given your own figure. **Decide, say why, and give the controller both figures.** Sometimes you can accept and sometimes you cannot. One question continues from the question before. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 20 or 30 seconds, as shown

body.text: Your maximum tailwind for landing is one five knots. You want the shorter routing if you can accept it.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, runway zero nine is available with a one zero knot tailwind, and it saves you one two minutes. Can you accept?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
You are heavy today. With the flaps you have out, the slowest speed you can hold is one eight zero knots.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, reduce speed to two one zero knots until one two miles. Can you do that?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
MAVIK

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, maintain two six zero knots or greater until MAVIK for spacing. Can you do that?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
Pembury / Dunmere

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Pembury RVR runway one eight is 450 metres and dropping. Dunmere RVR is 800 metres, one six minutes away. Say your intentions.
Say your intentions.
ZENTA

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, hold at ZENTA, left turns, maintain 8,000 feet, expect approach clearance at 1125Z.
It is now 1105Z and you are holding at ZENTA. Your fuel endurance is one hour one zero minutes and your diversion to Dunmere needs three five minutes. You would rather stay if your fuel allows it.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept that delay, or do you want to divert now?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
You are at 9,000 feet, still in heavy rain and moderate turbulence. You want to stay on heading one four zero for five more miles to get out of it.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the last cell cleared the field one zero minutes ago, so you should be clear of the weather now?
Respond accordingly and make a request with a reason.

sections.title: 약점 C. 값 유지 — 되묻기 롤플레이

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In Part C you will be interacting with an Air traffic controller through ten turns. **The controller will ask you for your figures later in the scenario, and some of them will have changed.** Follow the prompts and respond as necessary. "Say again (=Repeat)" available only once. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 30 seconds or less

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level two one zero, 60 miles from PERNO, inbound to Alderton Airport. Your fuel endurance is two hours three five minutes and there are one six three persons on board. Your required landing distance is 2,200 metres, and at today's weight the slowest speed you can hold is one eight zero knots.

body.text: Contact Alderton Approach, report your position and level, and request descent.
PERNO ONE arrival
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire about the freezing level.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Alderton Approach, descend to one one thousand, expect the PERNO ONE arrival, ILS runway two seven. Be advised, icing reported in cloud on the arrival.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and tell him what you can do instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the freezing level is 7,000 feet. Reduce speed to one six zero knots until one zero miles.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing 12,000 feet you get a WING ANTI-ICE FAULT caption for the left wing, and ice is building on that wing. You want to descend to 6,000 feet to get below the freezing level. Your slowest speed is now two zero zero knots and your required landing distance is now 2,700 metres.

body.text: Report your problem to the controller, tell him what has changed, and make a request with a reason.
Alderton / Wexcombe
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and state your decision with a reason.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, descend to 6,000 feet. Alderton runway two seven gives you 2,500 metres. Wexcombe has 3,000 metres and it's one two minutes away. What would you like?

pre.text: Situation Update You are now level at 6,000 feet, below the freezing level. There is still ice on the left wing. You want the fire service standing by as a precaution.

body.text: Listen to the controller and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, you're below the freezing level now, so I take it the ice has gone. Is that right, and do you want the fire service standing by?
Listen to the controller and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, understood. Wexcombe's asking for your fuel endurance and how many people you've got on board.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and tell him whether you can do that with a reason.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn right heading three zero zero, descend to 4,000 feet, reduce speed to two two zero knots. Can you do that speed? Contact Wexcombe Approach on 126.85.
You are now with a new controller who has none of your figures. Listen to him and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Wexcombe Approach, radar contact. I've got nothing on you yet — say your slowest speed and the number of persons on board.

pre.text: Situation Update The ice has now gone from the left wing. The fault remains, so your figures do not change.

body.text: Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and tell him about the ice and the fault.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn left heading zero niner zero, descend to 3,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway one two approach, contact Wexcombe Tower on 118.75.

sections.title: 약점 D. 발신 — 기관 호출 · REQUEST + 명사구

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In Part D you usually call first, with **no controller transmission.** Each situation tells you what you want. One question continues from the question before. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 20 seconds or less

body.text: Stanmore Control
Make a request with a reason.
Alderton Delivery / GOSMA TWO / LIDRO ONE
Report your situation and make a request.
ROLDA

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, reduce speed to two five zero knots until ROLDA.
Two minutes later you see that you selected the wrong speed by mistake. You are at two eight zero knots and nobody has said anything to you. You are reducing now. Contact Stanmore Control.
Report your status and say your intentions.
Dunmere
Make a request with a reason.
One minute ago, passing 5,000 feet, about five miles south of the field, a green laser from the ground lit up your cockpit. You want the controller to know about it. Contact Pembury Approach.
Make a report.
You are holding short of runway zero nine at Alderton. The oil quantity on engine number two is dropping. You want to go back to the stand. Contact Alderton Tower.
Report your status and make a request.

pre.text: ✅ Directions : You will be asked four questions about Part C. **You have up to 90 seconds for each.** Answer every part of the question.

body.text: Follow up question.

In this situation, you told the controller about the fault and what had changed. Which figures changed, and why did he need to know them? In your role as a pilot, how do you make sure you use the latest figure and not the old one? Give an example.
Follow up question.

In this situation, the controller thought the ice had gone, but it had not. Why was it important to correct him straight away? From your own experiences, how do you report a problem that is still going on? Give an example.

How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
